note: Track modes (theory-modes), step 1: Dorian, built from the minor pentatonic the player knows by adding the 2nd and the major 6th, with the 6th heard over a drone and then over a Dorian backing track in three keys.

exercise.title: Dorian: the minor pentatonic plus two notes
exercise.why: Dorian is the minor pentatonic with the 2nd and the major 6th added, and the 6th is the note that sets it apart from plain minor, so learn to hear that note against the root.

cells.text:
The staff below shows D Dorian. The plain notes are the D minor pentatonic, and the ringed {{2}} and {{6}} are the two notes Dorian adds.
Tap up the scale from {{1}}, then tap {{5}}, {{6}} and {{5}} to hear the major 6th beside its neighbour.

Press Play below to start the drone on D. Tap {{1}}, {{6}} and {{1}} on the staff against it, then tap short lines of your own that keep coming back to {{6}}.
Practice until you can hum {{6}} over the drone before you tap it.

Press Play below to start the backing track: two chords, the 1 and the 4, round and round. Tap lines of your own on the staff over it, and land on the ringed {{6}} when the second chord comes: it is that chord's 3rd.
Once the {{6}} lands with the chord, try another key. Use the Key selector below to change the key, then press Play to start the backing track again.
When you change the key, the notes are new but the ringed note is still the {{6}}.
